23125-the-love-affairs-of-pixie.title: The Love Affairs Of Pixie
23125-the-love-affairs-of-pixie.creator: Unknown
23125-the-love-affairs-of-pixie.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. When Pixie O'Shaughnessy had reached her twentieth birthday it was borne in upon her with the nature of a shock that she was not beautiful. Hitherto a buoyant and innocent self-satisfaction, coupled with the atmosphere of love and admiration by which she was surrounded in the family circle, had succeeded in blinding her eyes to the very obvious defects of feature which the mirror portrayed. But suddenly, sharply, her eyes were opened.

41593-unexplored-spain.title: Spain
41593-unexplored-spain.creator: Unknown
41593-unexplored-spain.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The Spain that we love and of which we write is not the Spain of tourist or globe-trotter. These hold main routes, the highways from city to city; few so much as venture upon the bye-ways. Our Spain begins where bye-ways end.

arxiv-2311-01319.title: MMP for locally stable families and wall crossing for moduli of stable pairs Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification : 14E30, 14J10, 14J17. Keywords : minimal model program, moduli spaces, stable pairs.
arxiv-2311-01319.creator: Fanjun Meng, Ziquan Zhuang
arxiv-2311-01319.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fanjun Meng, Ziquan Zhuang. We construct reduction and wall-crossing morphisms between the moduli spaces of stable pairs as the coefficients vary, generalizing the earlier work of Ascher, Bejleri, Inchiostro and Patakfalvi which deals with the klt case. Along the proof, we show that one can run the MMP with scaling on normal locally stable families over a normal base, and that the existence of good minimal models is preserved when reducing coefficients away from zero.

arxiv-2410-14816.title: Revisiting the Unicity Distance through a Channel Transmission Perspective
arxiv-2410-14816.creator: F. Lin
arxiv-2410-14816.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by F. Lin. - This paper revisits the classical notion of unicity distance from an enlightening perspective grounded in information theory, specifically by framing the encryption process as a noisy transmission channel. Using results from reliable communication theory, we derive a simple information-theoretic proof of the same unicity distance formula as in Shannon’s classical result and a channel transmission interpretation of the unicity distance.

arxiv-2508-03083.description: Abstract . Diffusion models have recently emerged as powerful tools for missing data imputation by modeling the joint distribution of observed and unobserved variables. However, existing methods, typically based on stochastic denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs), suffer from high inference latency and variable outputs, limiting their applicability in real-world tabular settings.

pmc-10537147.title: The Circadian Nobiletin-ROR Axis Suppresses Adipogenic Differentiation and IκBα/NF-κB Signaling in Adipocytes
pmc-10537147.creator: Eunju Kim, Kazuaki Mawatari, Seung-Hee Yoo, Zheng Chen, Sang J Chung
pmc-10537147.description: Obesity is a known risk factor for metabolic diseases and is often associated with chronic inflammation in adipose tissue. We previously identified the polyethoxylated flavonoid Nobiletin (NOB) as a circadian clock modulator that directly binds to and activates the ROR receptors in the core oscillator, markedly improving metabolic fitness in obese mice.

pmc-11373632.title: Impact of TP53 loss-of-function alterations on the response to PSMA radioligand therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients
pmc-11373632.creator: Peter H.J. Slootbeek, María Victoria Luna-Velez, Bastiaan M. Privé, Maarten J. van der Doelen, Iris S.H. Kloots, Samhita Pamidimarri Naga, Hilde E. Onstenk, James Nagarajah, Harm Westdorp, Inge M. van Oort, Leonie I. Kroeze, Jack. A. Schalken, Haiko J. Bloemendal, Niven Mehra
pmc-11373632.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Rationale: PSMA-targeting radioligand therapy (PSMA-RLT) has shown promise in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), particularly in PSMA-avid tumours. However, predicting response remains challenging. Preclinical data suggests aberrant p53-signalling as a predictor of poor response.Methods: The patient population of this pre-planned retrospective cohort study consists of 96 patients with mCRPC who underwent treatment with PSMA-RLT and were molecularly profiled by whole-genome sequencing and or targeted next-generation sequencing.

pmc-11532501.title: Lattice hydrogen transfer in titanium hydride enhances electrocatalytic nitrate to ammonia conversion
pmc-11532501.creator: Jiawei Li, Wanqiang Yu, Haifeng Yuan, Yujie Wang, Yuke Chen, Di Jiang, Tong Wu, Kepeng Song, Xuchuan Jiang, Hong Liu, Riming Hu, Man Huang, Weijia Zhou
pmc-11532501.description: The electrocatalytic reduction of nitrate toward ammonia under mild conditions addresses many challenges of the Haber-Bosch reaction, providing a sustainable method for ammonia synthesis, yet it is limited by sluggish reduction kinetics and multiple competing reactions. Here, the titanium hydride electrocatalyst is synthesized by electrochemical hydrogenation reconstruction of titanium fiber paper, which achieves a large ammonia yield rate of 83.

pmc-12550906.title: Modeling and Characterizing the Growth of the Texas–New Mexico Measles Outbreak of 2025
pmc-12550906.creator: Gilberto González-Parra, Annika Vestrand, Remy Mujynya
pmc-12550906.description: Background: In late January 2025, a measles outbreak began in Gaines County, Texas, USA, and the outbreak extended to New Mexico. We used a variety of mathematical models to estimate the growth rate of the Texas–New Mexico measles outbreak of 2025.

pmc-12610019.title: Predicting Pulmonary Exacerbations in Cystic Fibrosis Using Inflammation-Based Scoring Systems
pmc-12610019.creator: Raphael S Reitmeier, Melanie Götschke, Julia Walter, Jeremias Götschke, Julian Schlatzer, Diego Kauffmann-Guerrero, Jürgen Behr, Amanda Tufman, Pontus Mertsch, Costin Teodor Streba
pmc-12610019.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: The aim of this study is to identify people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) at risk for future pulmonary exacerbations (PEx) based on established and unestablished markers of chronic inflammation. There is currently no universal definition of PEx in cystic fibrosis (CF), but it is commonly characterized by clinical deterioration and a drop in FEV1 ≥10% with or without elevations in systemic inflammatory markers.

pmc-12619485.title: Association between systemic inflammation response index and advanced stages in U.S. cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome patients: a cross-sectional study using NHANES 2015–2020 data
pmc-12619485.creator: Jing Zhang, Dingyuan Tu
pmc-12619485.description: BackgroundThe American Heart Association introduced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, a highly prevalent multistage comorbidity in the U.S. We investigated the association between the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), a new inflammatory marker, and advanced CKM syndrome.MethodsUsing National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data (2015–2020), we classified U.S. adults into five CKM syndrome stages (0–4).

pmc-12748170.title: Hybrid approach: a prospective option for treating congenital heart defects in pediatric patients
pmc-12748170.creator: Shukhrat Marassulov, Oleg Lookin, Bakhytzhan Nurkeyev, Amangeldy Kerimkulov, Saniya Murzabayeva, Bauyrzhan Tuyakbayev, Raikhan Dochshanova, Rinat Maiorov, Assiya Akhmoldayeva, Elmira Kuandykova, Yerbol Aldabergenov, Timur Raimkhanov, Akkerbez Adilbekova
pmc-12748170.description: Congenital heart defects (CHDs), a life-threatening congenital pathology, are reported in approximately one out of every 100 live births, with the severity ranging from mild to fatal. The prevalence of CHDs has significantly increased over the last few decades, most likely due to evolved diagnostics and increased accessibility to healthcare worldwide.

pmc-13016605.title: Stall force measurement of the kinesin-3 motor KIF1A using a programmable DNA origami nanospring
pmc-13016605.creator: Nobumichi Takamatsu, Hiroko Furumoto, Takayuki Ariga, Mitsuhiro Iwaki, Kumiko Hayashi, Mohan K Balasubramanian, Nobumichi Takamatsu, Hiroko Furumoto, Takayuki Ariga, Mitsuhiro Iwaki, Kumiko Hayashi
pmc-13016605.description: DNA origami technology is a method for designing and constructing nanoscale structures using DNA, and it is being applied across various fields. This technology was advanced by developing the nanospring (NS), a fluorescently visible molecular spring that quantifies forces through its extension and has been used to measure myosin-generated forces.

pmc-13211040.title: Classical Phytohormones and Peptide Plant Hormones in Abiotic Stress Tolerance: Crosstalk, Physiological Integration, and Crop Improvement
pmc-13211040.creator: Baber Ali, Ayesha Imran, Hamza Iftikhar, Zeeshan Khan, Fozia Saeed, Zahid Hussain, Abdul Waheed, Arafat Abdel Hamed Abdel Latef, Nijat Imin
pmc-13211040.description: Plants are constantly exposed to a wide range of abiotic stresses that have significant negative impacts on growth and yield. Plant acclimation to these stresses is governed by integrated classical phytohormone and plant peptide hormone signalling networks that control the ability of a plant to survive and adapt to extreme environments.

pmc-13332624.title: Recurrent Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis With Aortomitral Curtain Destruction in an Elderly Patient
pmc-13332624.creator: Tea-Terezija Cvetko, Jasmina Ćatić, Jelena Kursar, Ivica Šafradin, Vlatka Rešković Lukšić, Ivana Jurin
pmc-13332624.description: BackgroundRecurrent prosthetic valve infective endocarditis in older adults can present atypically and progress rapidly, requiring complex decisions.Case SummaryA 69-year-old man with prior bioprosthetic aortic and mitral valve replacement presented with progressive back pain without fever. Blood cultures grew Enterococcus faecalis. Transesophageal echocardiography showed large vegetations on both prostheses with periannular extension and an aortic root abscess.

pmc-13503396.title: Head and Neck Rhabdomyosarcoma in Children: An Otolaryngological Perspective on Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approaches
pmc-13503396.creator: Agata Wojno, Milena Chmielewska, Sara Shefa, Oliwia Cichy, Paulina Lenkiewicz, Karolina Dorobisz
pmc-13503396.description: Purpose of ReviewHead and neck rhabdomyosarcoma (HNRMS) is the most common soft-tissue sarcoma in children, with approximately 30–40% of cases arising in the head and neck region. Due to its anatomical complexity, histopathological diversity, and molecular heterogeneity, HNRMS remains a major diagnostic and therapeutic challenge in pediatric otolaryngology.
